translations.text: We ask, almighty God, that through the power of the Holy Spirit you make us teachable in faith and steadfast in professing it, for you granted blessed Sixtus and his companions to lay down their lives for your word and the testimony of Jesus. Through our Lord Jesus Christ your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever.

new_entry.witness_note: Study English based on a complete Paris prayer attributed to 1738 in Gerard O’Connor’s 2004 scholarly transcription, adapted to include Sixtus’s companions. The original 1738 page and ending cue have not been checked. Dumas’s source list dates the Paris missal to 1736, while O’Connor identifies 1738; this discrepancy remains unresolved, so Dumas supplies only a Paris-source reference. The full conclusion is independently attested in an 1862 missal and selected by the cue and rule in a secondary witness of the 2002 Roman Missal. Correspondence with the complete controlling 2008 edition has not been established. Not an approved liturgical translation.

old_gap.note: The witness reaches this day and reaches it by reference. Read on the 1861 page image on 2026-08-20: leaf n543, printed p. 535, running head `13th AND 14th JANUARY.`, prints `XIV. St. HILARY, bp. c... All as in Mass XII. p. 485, with a Commem. of St. Felix, by the following Collect, &c.` The only oration printed under that heading is FELIX's commemoration (`COLLECT. Concede.--Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that the examples of thy saints may excite us to the amendment of our lives`), which is not this prayer. Mass XII is the witness's Mass of Doctors, whose orations print `N.` and, in the Secret and Postcommunion, name a Confessor where this calendar's Latin names a Bishop and Doctor. The roman-1962 overlay refused the same three slots on the same evidence on 2026-08-02 and this lane confirms it rather than reversing it. Nothing is carried. Incipit of the Latin refused here: `Deus, qui populo tuo`. Read on the page image https://archive.org/download/romanmissaltran00churgoog/page/n543_w1400.jpg (leaf n543, printed p. 535, heading `13th AND 14th JANUARY. / XIV. St. HILARY, bp. c.`) by lane pc-antecedent-english on 2026-08-20. The later unofficial-web rows were rejected as authoritative exemplars; their wording was quarantined and is represented only by the SHA-256 fingerprint above.

new_entry.ancient_reading: Dirige oves tuas, Domine, in viam salutis aeternae, quam beati Pontificis Damasi vita cum doctrina monstravit: et fac nos eodem intercedente, sic eius subsequi vestigia, ut cum ipso coronari mereamur.

translations.text: Guide your faithful, Lord, along the way of eternal salvation, which blessed Apollinaris the bishop showed by his teaching and martyrdom; and, through his intercession, make us so persevere in your commandments that we may be worthy to be crowned with him. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for all ages of ages.
